Third VERDANT governance review to examine final pilot evidence, approve conclusions on utility, privacy and operations, and agree recommendations for the next phase in 2027.

Andrés Beltrán: We will review accumulated evidence before operational closure on 30 November.
Inés Ferrer: Since May, 86,976 hourly records and eight local runs were processed. Hourly data retained more than 96 percent of the information required for the initial indicators.
Sergio Vidal: There were 158 requests: 147 approved and eleven rejected. No transfer breached granularity, purpose or retention. Every expired deletion is confirmed.
Nuria Castaño: Overall availability was 99.87 percent. The October drill revoked the compromised certificate in four minutes and restored authorized operation in nineteen.
Inés Ferrer: The daylight-saving transition generated no duplicates after UTC normalization. Missing data represented 3.6 percent, and dynamic suppression 4.3 percent.
Carmen Rey: SolCentro considers hourly data and local processing viable. It does not accept raw 15-minute export in the next phase.
Héctor Molina: The privacy assessment supports policy v1.0. For 2027, I recommend further automation of output controls, but not relaxing group-size minimums or purpose review.
Bruno Silva: The international partner proposes adding a second energy community, subject to an independent assessment and decision.
Javier Ortega: That expansion must be treated as new scope, with its own provider, purpose and access matrix.
Andrés Beltrán: Final conclusions are approved: aggregated hourly data and local processing are the authorized routes; export of raw 15-minute data remains prohibited. The current pilot will close on 30 November, and any 2027 expansion will require a new governance decision.
